intro: Judaism, Christianity and Islam are three of the world's biggest religions. They began in the same part of the world. All three tell stories about Abraham. All three teach that there is one God. Millions of people in Chicago follow one of them.

In this unit, you will visit a Passover table, an Easter church, and a Ramadan sunset. You will read short lines from the Torah, the Gospels and the Qur'an. You will learn what each tradition's people believe and do.

By the end, you will be able to name each tradition's holy book and main practices. You will explain what the three share and how they differ. And you will do it the way a scholar does: describe, do not judge.
bigQuestion: How are Judaism, Christianity and Islam alike, and how are they different?

test.q: Which three traditions are called Abrahamic?
test.why: All three tell stories about Abraham.

choices: The first five books of the Hebrew Bible
test.why: The Torah is the most important Jewish text.

test.q: Which holiday retells the story of Moses leading the Israelites from Egypt?
test.why: Passover remembers the escape from Egypt.
Shabbat runs from Friday sunset to Saturday night.

test.q: What do Christians believe about Jesus that Jews and Muslims do not?
choices: That he is the Son of God
test.why: Only Christians believe Jesus is the Son of God.

test.q: What does Easter celebrate for Christians?
choices: Their belief that Jesus rose from death
test.why: Easter celebrates the belief that Jesus rose.

test.q: Which book is scripture for Christians but not for Jews?
test.why: Jews do not read the New Testament as scripture.

test.q: Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant are families in which tradition?
test.why: These are the three big families of Christians.

test.q: Who do Muslims believe is God's last prophet?
test.why: Muslims believe Muhammad is the last prophet.

test.q: How many times a day do Muslims pray salat?
test.why: Salat is prayed five times a day.

test.q: Which pillar of Islam is the pilgrimage to Mecca?
test.why: The hajj is the fifth pillar.

test.q: Which city is holy to Jews, Christians and Muslims?
test.why: All three traditions call Jerusalem holy.

test.q: Where do many Jews pray and study?
test.why: A synagogue is a Jewish house of prayer.

test.q: Which pair are both meals tied to a holy time?
test.why: The seder is the Passover meal; iftar breaks the Ramadan fast.

test.q: Which is a respectful way to study religion at school?
choices: Only learn about your own religion
Describe what people believe, without judging
test.why: Scholars describe beliefs and practices without judging them.

write.prompt: All three traditions teach care for others. Use at least two texts from this unit, such as Leviticus 19:18, the Good Samaritan in Luke 10, or what the Qur'an says about fasting and giving. Explain what each tradition teaches about helping others and why.
tips: Name the text you use, like "Luke 10."
Say who believes it: "Christians believe…" or "In Islam…"
Compare. Show what is the same and what is different.
Do not say which religion is right.
Use unit words like covenant, zakat and Gospels.
